hero.subtitle: A warm, hands-on workshop around thiéboudiène, Senegal's national dish — discover the country through its food.

moments.text: Each workshop follows thiéboudiène from fresh produce to the moment everyone shares the meal.

market.title: The ingredients
market.text: Fish, vegetables, spices: learn to recognise them.

cook.text: The slow simmer that gives the rice its flavour.

share.title: The sharing
share.text: The dish in the middle — and the conversation begins.

teranga.title: Here, the guest comes first
teranga.text: In Senegal, no one eats alone. The dish is set in the middle of the table, everyone gathers around the bowl, and the guest is always served first. That welcoming spirit is what we share at every workshop.

about.title: A home, a culture, a way of welcoming
about.intro: Kër Téranga was born from a simple belief: the best way to understand a country is to sit at its table.

name.title: The meaning of our name
name.kerText: "home" in Wolof — the place where you welcome, gather and pass things on.
name.terangaText: Senegalese hospitality, a founding value made of generosity, sharing and respect for others.
name.together: Kër Téranga means "the house of hospitality": a place where every visitor is welcomed like family.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.text: To bring Senegalese culture to life through authentic, accessible and warm food experiences that celebrate local produce and the people who grow, sell and cook it.

vision.title: Our vision
vision.text: To become a reference for cultural and culinary tourism in Senegal, and a living embassy of Teranga for travellers from all over the world.

heritage.title: A dish recognised by UNESCO
heritage.text1: Born in the fishing communities of Saint-Louis, ceebu jën — often spelled thiéboudiène — became Senegal's national dish. Its recipe and techniques are traditionally handed down from mother to daughter, and it is shared from one large communal bowl, often eaten by hand.
heritage.text2: In December 2021, UNESCO inscribed “Ceebu jën, a culinary art of Senegal” on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity — recognising a dish that is also an affirmation of Senegalese identity.
